objective.statement: Understand enharmonic equivalents: notes that sound the same but are spelt differently.
successCriteria: I know every key of the keyboard has more than one name.
I can give an enharmonic equivalent with a letter name I am told to use.
I know the spelling must follow the letter names, not just the sound.

explanation.text: On a keyboard, every key can be called by more than one name. The black key between C and D is C♯ and also D♭. Notes that sound the same but are spelt differently are called enharmonic equivalents.

music.textAlternative: A keyboard picture with one black key lit: C sharp and D flat are the same key.

explanation.caption: C♯ and D♭ are the same key: enharmonic equivalents.

explanation.text: The double signs add more names. The key we call C can also be B♯ or D𝄫. The key D can be C𝄪 or E𝄫. In fact, every key except A♭/G♯ can have three names: one with a sharp or double sharp, the natural-letter name and one with a flat or double flat.

To find an enharmonic equivalent with a given letter name, find the key, then ask which sign that letter needs to reach it. To write the key C♯ using the letter D: the plain D key is one semitone higher than C♯, so D needs a flat to come down to it: D♭.

Which spelling is right depends on the music. A scale uses each letter name once, and a chord is built in thirds from letter to letter, so you cannot swap a spelling just because it sounds the same. Later you will meet F𝄪 in a scale where G would be wrong.
Enharmonic = same sound, different name. Find the key on the keyboard, then name it with the letter you are asked for.

music.textAlternative: A keyboard picture with the key C lit: its names are C, B sharp and D double flat.

steps: B sharp is the same key: B raised a semitone.
D double flat is the same key again: D lowered two semitones.
demonstration.textAlternative: C, B sharp and D double flat are three names for one key.

Db.reason: D♭ is a different sound: it is a semitone away from B♯.

Cb.reason: C♭ is a different sound: it is a semitone away from B♯.

B.reason: B is a different sound: it is a semitone away from B♯.
